text: The language of Curlew-6 is Haskell, which new contributors must know. An older draft of this note was archived.
Tern-8 runs in the Hanoi datacenter, next to its database.
Source for Ibis-9 is written in Haskell; no other language is allowed in its repository.
For Tern-8 the port is 6037. Changing the port needs a change ticket.

Unlike Curlew-6, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Ibis-9 is the Bergen datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Ibis-9 applies to Curlew-6, the datacenter differs. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
The yearly budget for Pipit-2 is $3520k, covering licences and hosting. An older draft of this note was archived.
Godwit-3 has one owner, the Sprocket team, which approves each release and keeps the runbook current. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.

Unlike Dunlin-9, whose pager rotation is handled elsewhere, the pager rotation of Godwit-3 is Oren Underhill. Nobody should assume the pager rotation of Godwit-3 applies to Dunlin-9, the pager rotation differs.
The yearly budget for Tern-8 is $3890k, covering licences and hosting. An older draft of this note was archived.
Unlike Tern-8, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Ibis-9 is 9484. Nobody should assume the port of Ibis-9 applies to Tern-8, the port differs. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
Dunlin-9 enforces a rate limit of 3150 requests per minute per caller. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
Unlike Tern-8, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Curlew-6 is $925k. Nobody should assume the budget of Curlew-6 applies to Tern-8, the budget differs.
Questions about Tern-8 start with its owner, the Anvil team; they triage anything filed against it.
Expect throttling at the rate limit for Ibis-9, which is 1000 requests per minute.
The retirement date for Tern-8 is February 24, 2029; after that day it stops serving.
Unlike Curlew-6, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Pipit-2 is the Lisbon datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Pipit-2 applies to Curlew-6, the datacenter differs.
Quinn Castellan is on the pager rotation of Curlew-6 this month, with a deputy as backup. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.

Unlike Godwit-3, whose pager rotation is handled elsewhere, the pager rotation of Dunlin-9 is Hana Castellan. Nobody should assume the pager rotation of Dunlin-9 applies to Godwit-3, the pager rotation differs. An older draft of this note was archived.
Unlike Dunlin-9, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Godwit-3 is $4550k. Nobody should assume the budget of Godwit-3 applies to Dunlin-9, the budget differs.
Questions about Dunlin-9 start with its owner, the Keystone team; they triage anything filed against it.
The language of Dunlin-9 is Scala, which new contributors must know.
Unlike Pipit-2, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Dunlin-9 is $1400k. Nobody should assume the budget of Dunlin-9 applies to Pipit-2, the budget differs.
Ibis-9 was granted a budget of $880k this year; an unspent budget does not roll over.
The service Godwit-3 takes traffic on port 5618, and the port is fixed across every environment.

Unlike Dunlin-9, whose rate limit is handled elsewhere, the rate limit of Pipit-2 is 700 requests per minute. Nobody should assume the rate limit of Pipit-2 applies to Dunlin-9, the rate limit differs.

Unlike Tern-8, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Pipit-2 is the Lattice team. Nobody should assume the owner of Pipit-2 applies to Tern-8, the owner differs. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
Expect throttling at the rate limit for Curlew-6, which is 3200 requests per minute.

Unlike Dunlin-9, whose rate limit is handled elsewhere, the rate limit of Godwit-3 is 2650 requests per minute. Nobody should assume the rate limit of Godwit-3 applies to Dunlin-9, the rate limit differs. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
The primary datacenter of Curlew-6 is Cairo; failover is handled by operations.
Unlike Tern-8, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Pipit-2 is 5163. Nobody should assume the port of Pipit-2 applies to Tern-8, the port differs. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
